# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot

    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

Now I'll provide a comprehensive code quality review of the schema changes:

---

## Prisma Schema Review

### Summary
The changes introduce reading level customization through user preferences and cached simplified content variants. The implementation is generally sound but has one critical issue and some important considerations.

---

## Strengths

✓ **Naming conventions**: All models use PascalCase (SimplifiedContent), fields use camelCase (readingLevel, sectionId)

✓ **Appropriate data types**: String for reading levels (categorical enum values), DateTime for audit fields

✓ **Composite unique constraint**: The `@@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])` constraint on SimplifiedContent prevents duplicate content variants for the same section/level combination—essential for cache integrity

✓ **Cascade delete strategy**: SimplifiedContent correctly cascades on section deletion, maintaining referential integrity

✓ **Clear separation of concerns**: SimplifiedContent is properly isolated as a derived/cached content model, not mixed with core Section data

✓ **Documentation**: Comment on User.readingLevel hints at valid values, helping future developers

---

## Issues

### Critical

❌ **Missing index on SimplifiedContent.readingLevel**

The composite unique constraint `@@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])` creates an index on both fields, but queries filtering by just `readingLevel` (common for content variants like "fetch all undergraduate content") won't benefit from an index.

**Impact**: High - Will cause full table scans when querying by reading level alone

**Recommendation**:
```prisma
@@index([readingLevel])
@@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])
```

---

### Important

⚠️ **Reading level is an unconstrained string**

Both `User.readingLevel` and `SimplifiedContent.readingLevel` are plain strings without validation. Comments suggest valid values ("undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"), but the database enforces no constraints.

**Risks**:
- Invalid values can be inserted (e.g., "PhD" with capital P, "graduate")
- Application code must validate—schema cannot be the source of truth
- Mismatched values between User and SimplifiedContent lookups will fail silently

**Recommendation**: Document the enum constraint in comments or implement application-level validation. Consider adding a check constraint if SQL Server supports it:
```prisma
// For documentation clarity
// Valid values: "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
readingLevel String @default("undergraduate")
```

Or, if using a dedicated enum table, create:
```prisma
model ReadingLevel {
  id   String   @id @default(cuid())
  name String   @unique // "undergraduate", "masters", "phd"
  // ... other fields
}
```

⚠️ **No index on SimplifiedContent.sectionId**

While `sectionId` is part of the unique constraint, applications likely query by `sectionId` alone when fetching all variants. The composite index `[sectionId, readingLevel]` helps but a separate index might optimize queries.

**Recommendation**: Add `@@index([sectionId])` for queries like "get all simplified versions of this section"

---

### Minor

ℹ️ **Consider adding timestamps for cache validation**

SimplifiedContent has `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, which is good. However, consider whether you need an `expiresAt` or `generatedByModelVersion` field to track if cached content needs regeneration after model updates.

ℹ️ **No backfill strategy documented**

New users will get `readingLevel = "undergraduate"` by default, but existing users won't have this field populated (or will have NULL if you're adding it to an existing schema). Plan for a migration to set defaults.

---

## Approval Status

❌ **Needs fixes before deployment**

**Must fix before merging:**
1. Add index on `SimplifiedContent.readingLevel` (critical for performance)

**Should fix before merging:**
2. Add application-level validation or document enum constraint for reading levels
3. Add index on `SimplifiedContent.sectionId` for query optimization

**Optional improvements:**
4. Plan and document migration strategy for existing users' readingLevel field

---

```prisma
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  sectionId    String
  readingLevel String   // Valid values: "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
  content      String   @db.NVarChar(Max)

  section Section @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([sectionId])
  @@index([readingLevel])
  @@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])
```

Now I'll provide a comprehensive code quality review of the schema changes:

---

## Prisma Schema Review

### Summary
The changes introduce reading level customization through user preferences and cached simplified content variants. The implementation is generally sound but has one critical issue and some important considerations.

---

## Strengths

✓ **Naming conventions**: All models use PascalCase (SimplifiedContent), fields use camelCase (readingLevel, sectionId)

✓ **Appropriate data types**: String for reading levels (categorical enum values), DateTime for audit fields

✓ **Composite unique constraint**: The `@@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])` constraint on SimplifiedContent prevents duplicate content variants for the same section/level combination—essential for cache integrity

✓ **Cascade delete strategy**: SimplifiedContent correctly cascades on section deletion, maintaining referential integrity

✓ **Clear separation of concerns**: SimplifiedContent is properly isolated as a derived/cached content model, not mixed with core Section data

✓ **Documentation**: Comment on User.readingLevel hints at valid values, helping future developers

---

## Issues

### Critical

❌ **Missing index on SimplifiedContent.readingLevel**

The composite unique constraint `@@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])` creates an index on both fields, but queries filtering by just `readingLevel` (common for content variants like "fetch all undergraduate content") won't benefit from an index.

**Impact**: High - Will cause full table scans when querying by reading level alone

**Recommendation**:
```prisma
@@index([readingLevel])
@@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])
```

---

### Important

⚠️ **Reading level is an unconstrained string**

Both `User.readingLevel` and `SimplifiedContent.readingLevel` are plain strings without validation. Comments suggest valid values ("undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"), but the database enforces no constraints.

**Risks**:
- Invalid values can be inserted (e.g., "PhD" with capital P, "graduate")
- Application code must validate—schema cannot be the source of truth
- Mismatched values between User and SimplifiedContent lookups will fail silently

**Recommendation**: Document the enum constraint in comments or implement application-level validation. Consider adding a check constraint if SQL Server supports it:
```prisma
// For documentation clarity
// Valid values: "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
readingLevel String @default("undergraduate")
```

Or, if using a dedicated enum table, create:
```prisma
model ReadingLevel {
  id   String   @id @default(cuid())
  name String   @unique // "undergraduate", "masters", "phd"
  // ... other fields
}
```

⚠️ **No index on SimplifiedContent.sectionId**

While `sectionId` is part of the unique constraint, applications likely query by `sectionId` alone when fetching all variants. The composite index `[sectionId, readingLevel]` helps but a separate index might optimize queries.

**Recommendation**: Add `@@index([sectionId])` for queries like "get all simplified versions of this section"

---

### Minor

ℹ️ **Consider adding timestamps for cache validation**

SimplifiedContent has `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, which is good. However, consider whether you need an `expiresAt` or `generatedByModelVersion` field to track if cached content needs regeneration after model updates.

ℹ️ **No backfill strategy documented**

New users will get `readingLevel = "undergraduate"` by default, but existing users won't have this field populated (or will have NULL if you're adding it to an existing schema). Plan for a migration to set defaults.

---

## Approval Status

❌ **Needs fixes before deployment**

**Must fix before merging:**
1. Add index on `SimplifiedContent.readingLevel` (critical for performance)

**Should fix before merging:**
2. Add application-level validation or document enum constraint for reading levels
3. Add index on `SimplifiedContent.sectionId` for query optimization

**Optional improvements:**
4. Plan and document migration strategy for existing users' readingLevel field

---

```prisma
model SimplifiedContent {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  sectionId    String
  readingLevel String   // Valid values: "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
  content      String   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  section Section @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([sectionId])
  @@index([readingLevel])
  @@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])
}
```

3. **Consistent Error Handling Pattern**: Both endpoints use the same try-catch pattern with appropriate error extraction (`err instanceof Error`), matching patterns used elsewhere in the codebase.

4. **Clear HTTP Status Codes**: Appropriate use of 400 for client errors (invalid input) and 500 for server errors.

5. **Documentation**: JSDoc comments clearly document what each endpoint does.

6. **Defensive Programming**: Uses nullish coalescing (`??`) to provide sensible defaults in the GET response.

### Issues

#### Critical

1. **Missing Authentication/Authorization**
   - **Location**: Both `GET` and `PUT` handlers
   - **Issue**: No authentication checks. Any user can call these endpoints to get/modify any user's preferences via `getDefaultUser()`. This is a security vulnerability.
   - **Impact**: In production, this would expose user data and allow unauthorized modifications.
   - **Expected**: Should verify the current authenticated user before allowing access.
   - **Note**: Comments in `src/lib/user.ts` indicate this is acknowledged as a development limitation ("This will be replaced with proper auth later"), but this is a critical gap for production readiness.

#### Important

1. **Incomplete Response Types**
   - **Location**: `PUT` endpoint (line 55)
   - **Issue**: Returns only `{ success: true }` without the updated data. Other endpoints (e.g., `POST /api/books`) return the created/updated resource.
   - **Better Practice**: Should return the updated user preferences for consistency and to allow clients to confirm the change:
     ```json
     { success: true, data: { readingLevel: "masters" } }
     ```

2. **Inconsistent Error Logging**
   - **Location**: Both handlers
   - **Issue**: Missing `console.error()` logging unlike other API routes in the codebase (see `/api/books/route.ts` line 35 and `/api/books/[slug]/route.ts` line 22).
   - **Impact**: Makes debugging production issues harder without error observability.

   - **Location**: `GET` handler (line 13)
   - **Issue**: Calls `getDefaultUser()` which auto-creates a user if missing, but doesn't catch potential database errors during this operation. The try-catch is broad but doesn't distinguish between different error types.
   - **Better Practice**: Should handle database connection failures separately or provide more context in error responses.

#### Minor

1. **Missing Type Annotation for Request Body**
   - **Location**: `PUT` handler, line 32
   - **Issue**: `body` is implicitly `any` after `req.json()`. Could explicitly type it:
     ```typescript
     const body = await req.json() as { readingLevel?: unknown }
     ```
   - **Impact**: Minor—validation catches incorrect types anyway, but explicit typing improves IDE support.

2. **Validation Check Order**
   - **Location**: Lines 36-40
   - **Issue**: Multiple separate checks for edge cases (`undefined`, `null`, empty string) before the array inclusion check. This is valid but could be simplified:
     ```typescript
     if (!readingLevel || typeof readingLevel !== 'string' || !VALID_LEVELS.includes(readingLevel)) {
     ```
   - **Impact**: Minimal—current approach is explicit and clear, just slightly verbose.

3. **Magic String in Error Message**

   - **Issue**: `VALID_LEVELS.join(', ')` is evaluated at runtime. While functional, the error message construction could be more defensive against edge cases.
   - **Better Practice**: Pre-computed string constant or more robust string building.

- Consistent with other API routes in the codebase (pattern matching `/api/books/route.ts` structure)
- Proper use of destructuring and async/await
- Consistent status code naming conventions

# Code Quality Review: `src/app/api/section/[id]/simplified/route.ts`

## Overview
This is a Next.js 13+ App Router API endpoint that checks for cached simplified content at different reading levels. It's a straightforward read-only endpoint with minimal logic.

---

## STRENGTHS

1. **Type Safety**
   - Proper use of const assertion for `VALID_LEVELS` creating a readonly tuple
   - Derived `ReadingLevel` type from the const array (ensures single source of truth)
   - Correct TypeScript patterns with `as const`

2. **Input Validation**
   - Validates `level` query parameter against whitelist before use
   - Returns clear error message with valid options when validation fails
   - Appropriate 400 status code for bad requests

3. **Efficient Prisma Query**
   - Uses composite unique index `[sectionId, readingLevel]` via `findUnique()` instead of `findFirst()`
   - Leverages `select` to only fetch required field (`content`), reducing payload
   - Compound key lookup is optimal for cache hit/miss checks

4. **Error Handling**
   - Try-catch wrapper around entire endpoint
   - Graceful error message extraction with fallback
   - Returns 500 status for server errors

5. **Next.js Patterns**
   - Correct async function signature with `params` destructuring
   - Uses `NextResponse.json()` for consistent response formatting
   - Proper REST semantics (GET for read-only operation)

6. **Code Clarity**
   - Well-documented endpoint with JSDoc comment showing URL and query parameter
   - Clear response structure with `success` flag and differentiated `data` payloads
   - Explicit cached/not-cached distinction in response

---

## ISSUES

### CRITICAL

**1. Input Validation Type Coercion (Line 14)**
```typescript
const level = (url.searchParams.get('level') ?? 'undergraduate') as ReadingLevel
```

**Problem:** The type assertion `as ReadingLevel` bypasses type checking. The null-coalescing operator provides a default, but there's still a logic flaw: if a user provides an *invalid* level (e.g., `?level=invalid`), the `as ReadingLevel` assertion forces TypeScript to trust this is valid, then validation catches it at runtime.

**Impact:** While functional, this pattern is fragile and masks the intent. The validation comes *after* the unsafe assertion.

**Fix:** Validate first, then safely cast:
```typescript
const levelParam = url.searchParams.get('level') ?? 'undergraduate'
if (!VALID_LEVELS.includes(levelParam as any)) {
  return NextResponse.json(...) // early return
}
const level: ReadingLevel = levelParam as ReadingLevel // now safe
```

---

### IMPORTANT

**1. Missing Section ID Validation (Line 26)**
```typescript
sectionId: params.id,
```

**Problem:** The `params.id` is a dynamic route parameter. Unlike query parameters, there's no validation that it's a valid CUID or that the section exists. If an invalid ID is provided, the database query will simply return `null`, and the endpoint returns success with `{ cached: false }`. This could mask issues.

**Impact:** A malformed `sectionId` won't error—it silently returns "not cached." This inconsistency with the query parameter validation is confusing.

**Recommendation:** Consider adding validation for `params.id` format or add database error handling. Alternatively, document this behavior explicitly.

**2. Comparison with Related Code (Line 5)**
```typescript
const VALID_LEVELS = ['undergraduate', 'masters', 'phd'] as const
```

In `/api/user/preferences/route.ts`, the same constant is defined with identical values. This creates **duplication**.

**Impact:** Medium—if reading levels change, both places must be updated. A breaking change risk.

**Recommendation:** Extract `VALID_LEVELS` to a shared constants file (e.g., `lib/constants.ts` where `PHASES` is used in other routes).

---

### MINOR

**1. Incomplete Error Handling (Line 45)**
```typescript
const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to check cache'
```

**Problem:** This is good defensive coding, but in a TypeScript codebase, non-Error throws should be exceptionally rare. The fallback message is generic and doesn't help debugging unknown error types.

**Recommendation:** Consider logging the raw error for debugging:
```typescript
const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to check cache'
if (!(err instanceof Error)) {
  console.error('Unexpected error type:', err)
}
```

**2. Missing Logging (Entire Endpoint)**
```typescript
// No logging of cache hits/misses
```

**Problem:** For a caching layer, there's no observability. In production, you can't track cache effectiveness without logs.

**Recommendation:** Add optional debug logging:
```typescript
console.debug(`Cache check: section=${params.id}, level=${level}, cached=${!!cached}`)
```

**3. No TypeScript Runtime Safety on `params`**
```typescript
export async function GET(req: Request, { params }: { params: { id: string } })
```

**Problem:** The `params` object has an `id` property, but this isn't type-checked at runtime by Next.js. If the route changed to `[id]/[other]`, `params.id` would still type-check but fail at runtime.

**Recommendation:** This is a known Next.js limitation and not a code smell in isolation, but be aware when refactoring routes.

---

## Response Structure Analysis

The endpoint has two success paths:

1. **Cache Hit:** `{ success: true, data: { cached: true, content: "..." } }`
2. **Cache Miss:** `{ success: true, data: { cached: false } }`

This design is slightly unusual—returning `success: true` for a cache miss might confuse clients. Consider:

```typescript
// Alternative (more explicit)
{ success: true, cached: true, content: "..." }  // hit
{ success: true, cached: false }                  // miss
```

Current design is fine but less scannable.

---

## Testing Considerations

No automated tests present. Key scenarios to cover:

- Valid levels: `undergraduate`, `masters`, `phd`
- Invalid level: returns 400
- Missing level parameter: defaults to `undergraduate`
- Section exists in cache: returns content
- Section doesn't exist in cache: returns cache miss
- Invalid section ID: returns cache miss (implicit current behavior)
- Database errors: returns 500

---

**✅ CONDITIONAL APPROVAL WITH RECOMMENDATIONS**

### Approval Status
**NEEDS MINOR FIXES** (not critical blockers, but should be addressed before production)

### Must-Do
1. Fix the type assertion pattern (CRITICAL validation logic)
2. Extract `VALID_LEVELS` to shared constants

### Should-Do
3. Add validation or documentation for `params.id`
4. Consider adding debug logging for cache observability

### Nice-To-Have
5. Improve error fallback logging
6. Add comprehensive test coverage

## Code Quality Review: `src/app/api/section/[id]/simplified/stream/route.ts`

### Strengths ✅

1. **Proper SSE Format Implementation**
   - Correctly uses Server-Sent Events format with `text/event-stream` content type
   - Proper header setup: `no-cache`, `keep-alive` for connection persistence
   - Valid `data: {...}\n\n` format for each event

2. **Input Validation**
   - Strong type safety with `ReadingLevel` union type and `VALID_LEVELS` validation
   - Validates query parameter against allowlist before processing
   - Rejects invalid levels early with 400 response

3. **Error Handling Strategy**
   - Try-catch-finally block properly closes stream in all paths
   - Distinguishes between error types (Error vs unknown)
   - Sends error events to client before closing stream

4. **Data Processing**
   - Sensible paragraph splitting logic (handles CRLF/LF cross-platform)
   - Trims and filters empty paragraphs
   - Sends progress updates (`total` count, `paragraph` index)

5. **Database Caching**
   - Intelligently caches simplified content after successful generation
   - Uses proper upsert pattern with composite key
   - Only saves after all paragraphs processed

6. **TypeScript Types**
   - Interfaces clearly document event structure
   - Proper type annotations on stream controller
   - Const assertion for `VALID_LEVELS`

---

### Critical Issues ❌

1. **Fire-and-Forget Async Pattern Creates Unhandled Promise**
   ```typescript
   ;(async () => { ... })()  // Line 56-128
   ```
   **Problem:** The IIFE is not awaited. If the function throws an error that escapes the try-catch (highly unlikely here, but possible in evolution), it becomes an unhandled promise rejection.
   
   **Impact:** Potential unhandled rejection warnings in logs, difficult to debug, violates Node.js best practices.
   
   **Fix:** Store the promise and add `.catch()` handler, or use a wrapper function that handles all exceptions:
   ```typescript
   const generationPromise = (async () => { ... })()
   generationPromise.catch((err) => {
     console.error('Unhandled error in stream generation:', err)
   })
   ```

2. **Resource Leak on Client Disconnect**
   ```typescript
   return new Response(stream, { ... })  // Line 130
   ```
   **Problem:** If the client disconnects before stream completes, the background generation continues running—wasting API calls and database queries. There's no way to detect client disconnection and abort the operation.
   
   **Impact:** High resource consumption with dropped clients, potential database load from unnecessary inserts.
   
   **Fix:** Use `ReadableStream` abort signals to handle client disconnects:
   ```typescript
   const controller = new AbortController()
   stream.cancel().then(() => controller.abort())
   // Pass controller to generateText() to implement cancellation
   ```

---

### Important Issues ⚠️

1. **No Request Validation for `params.id`**
   ```typescript
   export async function GET(req: Request, { params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
   ```
   **Problem:** `params.id` is treated as trusted string without validation. No check for:
   - Empty string
   - Extremely long strings (potential DoS)
   - Special characters/injection attempts
   
   **Impact:** Could enable NoSQL injection or malformed database queries if Prisma isn't configured defensively.
   
   **Recommendation:** Validate section ID format (UUID, numeric, etc.) before database query.

2. **Large Paragraph Processing Memory Accumulation**
   ```typescript
   const simplifiedParagraphs: string[] = []  // Line 57
   // ... stored in memory for every paragraph
   simplifiedParagraphs.push(simplified.trim())  // Line 97
   ```
   **Problem:** Simplified content is kept in memory until all paragraphs are processed, then joined. For a 1000-paragraph section, this could be substantial memory overhead.
   
   **Impact:** Memory growth proportional to content size; potential OOM on large sections.
   
   **Recommendation:** Either stream directly to database or implement a streaming database write pattern instead of buffering.

3. **No Timeout Handling on Individual Paragraph Generation**
   ```typescript
   const simplified = await generateText({ ... })  // Line 91
   ```
   **Problem:** If `generateText()` hangs (network issue, Azure timeout), the request waits indefinitely. No timeout specified for individual API calls.
   
   **Impact:** Requests can hang indefinitely, consuming connection resources.
   
   **Recommendation:** Add timeout to fetch in `generateText()` (currently missing):
   ```typescript
   const controller = new AbortController()
   const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 30000)
   await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal, ... })
   ```

4. **Missing Status Code on Successful Response**
   ```typescript
   return new Response(stream, { ... })  // Line 130
   ```
   **Problem:** No explicit `status: 200` in response. While it defaults to 200, it's better to be explicit.
   
   **Impact:** Minor - response will work but best practice violation.

---

### Minor Issues 📋

1. **Inconsistent Error Event Structure**
   - Error events send `{ error: string }` 
   - Success sends `{ paragraph, text, done, total }` as separate events
   - Client must handle mixed event types
   - **Recommendation:** Document event contract or use discriminated union pattern

2. **No Logging for Observability**
   - No logs for stream start, completion, or failures
   - Difficult to debug production issues
   - **Recommendation:** Add structured logging (especially around database upsert, stream lifecycle)

3. **Prompt Template Mutation Inefficiency**
   ```typescript
   const prompt = promptConfig.template
     .replaceAll('{level}', level)
     .replaceAll('{paragraph}', paragraph)
   ```
   - Performs 2 replaceAll operations per paragraph (O(n) string operations)
   - For 1000 paragraphs = 2000 string scans
   - **Recommendation:** Use safer template function: `template.replace(/{level}/g, level)`

4. **No Content Validation**
   - Section content could be empty string after trim (filtered later but wastefully processed)
   - No maximum section size check (could cause OOM trying to split huge content)
   - **Recommendation:** Add early validation on section size

5. **Generic Error Message Leakage**
   ```typescript
   send({ error: message })  // Line 124
   ```
   - May expose internal Azure error details to client
   - **Recommendation:** Sanitize error messages for production

---

### Security Assessment

1. **Query Parameter Injection**: Protected by allowlist validation ✅
2. **NoSQL Injection**: Vulnerable - no ID validation ⚠️
3. **XSS (JSON encoding)**: Safe - `JSON.stringify` escapes properly ✅
4. **DoS via large payload**: Partially vulnerable - no content size limits ⚠️
5. **Information Disclosure**: Minor - error messages could be sanitized ⚠️

---

### Async Patterns Assessment

| Pattern | Status | Issue |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Fire-and-forget IIFE | ❌ | No error handling on promise |
| Stream closure | ✅ | Proper finally block |
| Database transaction | ✅ | Upsert is atomic |
| Error propagation | ⚠️ | Sends to client but doesn't log |

---

**Status: ⚠️ Needs Fixes**

### Must Fix (Blocking)
1. **Fire-and-forget promise** - Add `.catch()` handler to prevent unhandled rejection
2. **Client disconnect handling** - Implement abort signal to stop background generation

### Should Fix (Important)
3. Validate `params.id` before database query
4. Add timeout handling to `generateText()` calls
5. Reduce memory accumulation of simplifiedParagraphs

### Nice to Have (Minor)
- Add structured logging for observability
- Sanitize error messages
- Add explicit `status: 200`
- Improve template substitution efficiency

### Overall Assessment
The SSE implementation itself is well-structured with proper header configuration and event formatting. However, the background task pattern introduces critical resource management issues (unhandled promise, no client disconnect detection) and the missing parameter validation creates a security gap. These should be addressed before production deployment.

## Code Quality Review: Reading Level Changes in `src/app/settings/page.tsx`

### Overview
This is a new Settings page component that manages prompt configurations and reading level preferences. The reading level feature allows users to select from three tiers (Undergraduate, Masters, PhD) that control content simplification levels.

---

### STRENGTHS

1. **Clean React Patterns**
   - Proper use of `useState` for local state management
   - Well-organized `useEffect` hooks with single responsibility
   - Semantic component structure with clear sections

2. **Type Safety**
   - Good use of TypeScript interfaces (`Prompt` interface)
   - Proper typing for state: `Record<string, Prompt>`, `{ type: 'success' | 'error'; text: string } | null`
   - Accurate type annotations throughout

3. **UX Consistency**
   - Radio button group pattern matches existing codebase conventions (similar to `SectionTabs.tsx`)
   - Visual feedback with hover states and active states
   - Color-coded messages (green for success, red for error)
   - Disabled state handling prevents multiple submissions

4. **Error Handling**
   - Try-catch blocks in all async operations
   - Graceful fallbacks with console.error logging
   - User-facing error messages with sensible defaults
   - Finally blocks ensure cleanup (state reset)

5. **Responsive UI**
   - Proper use of Tailwind classes for layout
   - Accessible form controls with proper labels
   - Clear visual hierarchy with descriptions

6. **API Integration**
   - Clean separation of concerns (separate handlers for prompts vs reading level)
   - Proper HTTP methods (GET, PUT)
   - Correct Content-Type headers

---

### ISSUES

#### CRITICAL

1. **Race Condition in useEffect (Lines 30-58)**
   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     async function loadPrompts() { ... }
     loadPrompts()
     
     async function loadPreferences() { ... }
     loadPreferences()
   }, [])
   ```
   Both async functions fire simultaneously without dependencies. If one fails, there's no coordination. Both should complete independently, which is fine, but the pattern could be clearer. **No blocking issue**, but could be improved.

2. **No Validation of Reading Level on Client (Line 221)**
   ```tsx
   onChange={(e) => handleSaveReadingLevel(e.target.value)}
   ```
   The radio button values are hardcoded strings. If these don't match the backend's `VALID_LEVELS` in `/api/user/preferences/route.ts`, validation fails. The backend validates (`['undergraduate', 'masters', 'phd']`), which is good, but there's no explicit client-side validation or type safety linking the UI values to backend constants.

#### IMPORTANT

3. **Inconsistent Error Messaging (Lines 73, 96)**
   ```tsx
   setMessage({ type: 'error', text: json.error || 'Failed to save' })
   ```
   For `handleSaveReadingLevel`, if the backend returns a detailed error like "Invalid readingLevel. Must be one of: undergraduate, masters, phd", this is shown to the user. While informative, it's technical. Consider sanitizing or providing more user-friendly messages.

4. **Missing Loading State for Reading Level (Line 27)**
   ```tsx
   const [savingLevel, setSavingLevel] = useState(false)
   ```
   The `savingLevel` state disables the radio button during save (line 222), which is good UX. However, there's no visual indicator (like a spinner or "saving..." text) showing what's happening. Users won't know if it's loading or just disabled.

5. **Auto-Dismiss Messages Without Cancellation (Lines 79, 102)**
   ```tsx
   setTimeout(() => setMessage(null), 3000)
   ```
   Messages disappear after 3 seconds automatically. If a user is reading an error message, it disappears. No way to keep it visible. Also, timeout IDs aren't stored, so if the component unmounts, the timeout still fires (memory leak potential).

6. **Hardcoded Radio Button Values (Lines 203-206)**
   ```tsx
   { value: 'undergraduate', label: 'Undergraduate', desc: '...' },
   { value: 'masters', label: 'Masters', desc: '...' },
   { value: 'phd', label: 'PhD', desc: '...' },
   ```
   These should be extracted to a constant to avoid duplication with the backend's `VALID_LEVELS`. If backend changes, the UI won't update.

#### MINOR

7. **Unused `loading` State (Line 23)**
   The `loading` state for prompts is set but only used in the ternary on line 141. If the API call fails, `loading` becomes `false` and users see "Prompt not found" instead of an error message. Consider distinguishing between "loading" and "error" states for better UX.

8. **No Accessibility Labels**
   ```tsx
   <input type="radio" ... className="mt-1" />
   ```
   The radio input is inside a label, which is good, but the `name` attribute ("readingLevel") should ideally be unique per instance in case of multiple forms. This is fine for a single form but not scalable.

9. **Unnecessary String Escape in JSX (Line 159)**
   ```tsx
   (Use {'{variable}'} for placeholders)
   ```
   Using escaped braces is correct here to show literal `{variable}`, but it's a minor readability issue. The intent is clear but slightly awkward.

10. **No Loading State Initialization (Line 26)**
    ```tsx
    const [readingLevel, setReadingLevel] = useState<string>('undergraduate')
    ```
    Defaults to 'undergraduate', but the actual user preference is loaded asynchronously. If the user has a different preference, there's a brief flash of the wrong value. Consider initializing to `null` or showing a loading state.

---

### CONSISTENCY WITH CODEBASE

1. **Tab Navigation Pattern** - Matches `SectionTabs.tsx` well
2. **Error Handling** - Consistent with existing API call patterns
3. **Styling** - Matches Tailwind and color palette usage
4. **Component Structure** - Aligns with other page components

---

### TESTING RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Test reading level persists across page reloads
2. Test error handling when API calls fail
3. Test that invalid reading levels are rejected by backend
4. Test message auto-dismiss functionality
5. Test radio button accessibility with screen readers
6. Test simultaneous prompt and preference loading

---

### VERDICT

**⚠️ NEEDS FIXES (Before Merge)**

**Critical Issues to Address:**
1. Create a shared constant for valid reading levels (client + server)
2. Fix message auto-dismiss timeout cleanup (prevent memory leaks)
3. Add visual indicator for reading level save state
4. Handle loading vs. error states for preferences distinctly
5. Improve error message user-friendliness

**After fixes: APPROVED**

---

**Recommendation:** Address the 5 critical/important items above before merging. The code is functionally sound but has several small UX and maintainability gaps that are easy to fix.

## Code Quality Review: Simplification Toggle Changes in SectionTabs.tsx

**Commit:** `3abf7a8` - "feat: add Original/Simplified toggle to Read tab"
**File:** `/Users/varunr/projects/edps-web/src/app/book/[slug]/section/[num]/SectionTabs.tsx`

---

### STRENGTHS

**1. React Hooks & State Management**
- Well-organized state groups with clear comments (Lines 103-131): Recall state, Quiz state, Evaluation state, and Read view state are distinctly separated
- Appropriate use of `useRef` for EventSource cleanup and debounce timers
- Correct dependency arrays in useEffect hooks to prevent infinite loops
- Proper initialization refs to prevent autosave on mount (Lines 139-140, 255-256)

**2. EventSource Handling** 
- Excellent defensive programming for EventSource management (Lines 133-134, 311-318):
  - Proper cleanup on unmount to prevent memory leaks
  - Explicit ref nulling after closing to avoid dangling references
  - Dual-closure pattern both in handler and in finally cleanup
- Safe EventSource re-initialization (Lines 379-382): Explicitly closes and nulls previous instance before creating new one
- Comprehensive error handling with `onmessage` and `onerror` listeners (Lines 426-461)

**3. Error Handling**
- Multiple error resilience patterns:
  - Try-catch blocks around async operations (Lines 390-413, 420-465)
  - Graceful fallbacks for failed preference fetches (Lines 390-399)
  - User-friendly error messages (Line 457, 463)
  - Network error recovery with "Try again" button (Lines 573-578)
- Proper error state management with `simplifyError` state (Line 131)
- Distinction between cache check errors and generation errors

**4. TypeScript Usage**
- Strong typing with well-defined interfaces (Lines 26-74):
  - `RecallAnswers`, `Question`, `EvaluationData` types are comprehensive
  - Discriminated union for `ReadView` type (Line 77): 'original' | 'simplified'
  - `SimplifyStatus` type correctly models async operation states (Line 78)
- Proper use of type guards and null checks throughout
- Type-safe callback with `useCallback` return type inference

**5. UI/UX Patterns**
- Progressive content display during streaming (Lines 580-593):
  - Shows paragraphs as they arrive
  - Displays "Simplifying X/Y" progress indicator
  - Skeleton loader with animate-pulse for better perceived performance
- Smart toggle behavior (Lines 372-376): Clicking same button returns to original view
- Reading level badge displayed only when simplified is ready (Lines 552-556)
- Cache hit optimization: Returns immediately if content cached (Lines 406-410)
- Comprehensive progress states: idle, loading, ready, error (Line 78)

**6. Data Flow Architecture**
- Clean separation between preference loading and simplification generation
- Two-step cache checking pattern: Prevents unnecessary regeneration
- EventSource streaming allows incremental paragraph display vs. waiting for entire response
- State mutations are atomic and avoid race conditions

---

### ISSUES

#### **CRITICAL**

**1. Race Condition in Simplification Stream (Lines 426-446)**
```typescript
eventSource.onmessage = (event) => {
  const data = JSON.parse(event.data)
  if (data.paragraph !== undefined && data.text) {
    setSimplifiedParagraphs((prev) => {
      const updated = [...prev]
      updated[data.paragraph] = data.text  // ⚠️ INDEX-BASED MUTATION
      return updated
    })
  }
}
```
- **Problem**: If paragraphs arrive out-of-order or with duplicates, sparse array mutation could create gaps or overwrite previous data
- **Impact**: Could result in missing or scrambled paragraphs in the final output
- **Fix**: Consider using Map or object keying: `{ [data.paragraph]: data.text }`

**2. Unvalidated EventSource Data Parsing (Line 427)**
```typescript
const data = JSON.parse(event.data)
```
- **Problem**: No error handling for malformed JSON from server
- **Impact**: Single malformed event could crash the component silently (caught by nothing)
- **Likelihood**: Medium - if API changes or network corruption occurs
- **Fix**: Wrap in try-catch or validate schema

#### **IMPORTANT**

**1. Reading Level Preference Re-fetched Every Toggle (Lines 389-399)**
```typescript
let currentLevel = readingLevel
try {
  const prefRes = await fetch('/api/user/preferences')
  const prefJson = await prefRes.json()
  if (prefJson.success) {
    currentLevel = prefJson.data.readingLevel
    setReadingLevel(currentLevel)
  }
} catch (err) {
  console.error('Failed to fetch reading level:', err)
}
```
- **Problem**: Makes unnecessary API call to /api/user/preferences every time simplified view is clicked
- **Context**: There's already a separate useEffect loading preferences on mount (Lines 296-309)
- **Impact**: Network overhead, slight UX delay, inconsistent with "preference already loaded" pattern
- **Suggestion**: Only re-fetch if explicitly changed in settings, or use cached value. If re-fetching is intentional for freshness, consider debouncing

**2. No Validation of Server Response Data Types (Multiple locations)**
```typescript
if (data.total !== undefined) setTotalParagraphs(data.total)  // Line 438
if (data.paragraph !== undefined && data.text) {...}         // Line 441
if (data.done) setSimplifyStatus('ready')                     // Line 449
```
- **Problem**: No validation that `data.total` is a number, `data.paragraph` is a valid integer, or `data.text` is a string
- **Impact**: Type mismatches could silently produce unexpected UI (e.g., `totalParagraphs` could be string "100")
- **Fix**: Add runtime validation: `typeof data.total === 'number' && data.total > 0`

**3. Stale Content Display on Toggle Back (Lines 384-386)**
```typescript
setReadView('simplified')
setSimplifyError(null)
setSimplifiedContent('') // Clear stale content
```
- **Problem**: `simplifiedContent` is cleared but `simplifiedParagraphs` array isn't reset if switching from cached to new generation
- **Scenario**: User toggles to simplified (cached), then toggles to original, then toggles back to simplified (requires new generation). The old cached paragraphs might still be in array
- **Impact**: Could briefly show old paragraphs mixed with new ones during streaming
- **Fix**: Also reset: `setSimplifiedParagraphs([])` at line 385

**4. Missing Abort Signal for Preference Fetch (Lines 391-396)**
```typescript
const prefRes = await fetch('/api/user/preferences')
const prefJson = await prefRes.json()
if (prefJson.success) {
  currentLevel = prefJson.data.readingLevel
}
```
- **Problem**: If component unmounts or user clicks button again before this completes, no way to cancel the request
- **Impact**: Memory leak potential (state update on unmounted component), network request waste
- **Mitigation Exists?** Partial - unmount cleanup exists for EventSource, not for this fetch
- **Fix**: Use AbortController and pass signal to fetch

---

#### **MINOR**

**1. Loose Error Suppression (Lines 304-305, 398)**
```typescript
} catch (err) {
  console.error('Failed to load reading level:', err)
}
```
- **Pattern**: Silently continues with stale `readingLevel` if preference fetch fails
- **UX Impact**: User may not know their preference wasn't applied; simplification happens with outdated level
- **Severity**: Low - has sensible fallback (use state value), but silent failures can be confusing
- **Improvement**: Consider warning toast or UI feedback

**2. Magic String in URL Construction (Lines 403, 422)**
```typescript
`/api/section/${sectionId}/simplified?level=${currentLevel}`
`/api/section/${sectionId}/simplified/stream?level=${currentLevel}`
```
- **Issue**: Query parameter encoding not verified; if `currentLevel` has special characters, could break URL
- **Likelihood**: Very low (only enum-like values: 'elementary', 'high_school', 'undergraduate', 'graduate')
- **Best Practice**: Use `URLSearchParams` for robustness

**3. Inconsistent Success Flag Checking (Line 404, 301)**
```typescript
// Line 301 checks: if (json.success)
// Line 404 checks: if (cacheJson.success && cacheJson.data.cached)
// Both missing null/undefined checks on json.data before accessing
```
- **Risk**: If API returns `{success: true, data: null}`, accessing `json.data.cached` throws
- **Mitigation**: Unlikely in controlled API, but defensive programming missing
- **Fix**: Add `cacheJson.data?.cached`

**4. No Connection Timeout Handling (Line 421-423)**
```typescript
const eventSource = new EventSource(
  `/api/section/${sectionId}/simplified/stream?level=${currentLevel}`
)
```
- **Issue**: EventSource has default timeout, but no explicit timeout/reconnection strategy
- **Scenario**: If server responds slowly or has network latency, user sees loading indefinitely
- **Standard Practice**: Set timeout or implement manual heartbeat

**5. Inconsistent Error Messages (Lines 457, 463)**
```typescript
setSimplifyError('Connection lost. Please try again.')     // onerror handler
setSimplifyError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to generate')  // catch block
```
- **Issue**: Different error message styles; first is user-friendly, second is developer-friendly
- **UX Impact**: Confusing to user if they see technical error message
- **Fix**: Normalize error messages for user consumption

---

### CODE METRICS

| Metric | Status | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| **Hook Dependency Arrays** | ✅ CORRECT | All dependencies properly listed; no stale closures detected |
| **Ref Cleanup** | ✅ CORRECT | EventSource cleanup on unmount is thorough |
| **Memory Leaks** | ⚠️ POTENTIAL | Unaborted fetch in preference loading could leak |
| **Type Safety** | ✅ STRONG | Comprehensive interface definitions; mostly sound type usage |
| **Error Boundaries** | ⚠️ INCOMPLETE | try-catch exists but JSON parsing not protected |
| **EventSource Lifecycle** | ✅ GOOD | Multiple layers of defensive cleanup |
| **State Organization** | ✅ EXCELLENT | Clear grouping with comments; 130 lines well-structured |
| **UI Responsiveness** | ✅ GOOD | Streaming display and progress indicator provide good UX |

---

## VERDICT

**Status: ⚠️ NEEDS FIXES (Critical and Important issues present)**

### Summary

The simplification toggle implementation demonstrates **strong architectural thinking** with well-organized state, proper EventSource cleanup, and good UI patterns. However, **three critical/important issues** must be addressed:

1. **Race condition in paragraph array mutation** - Could produce incorrect output
2. **Unprotected JSON parsing** - Silent crashes possible
3. **Unnecessary preference re-fetch** - Network overhead and UX latency
4. **Stale state not fully cleared** - Could show old data briefly

### Recommended Actions Before Merge

**Must Fix (Blocking):**
- [ ] Wrap `JSON.parse(event.data)` in try-catch (Line 427)
- [ ] Fix array index mutation race condition (Lines 441-446) - use object/Map keying
- [ ] Reset `simplifiedParagraphs` when starting new generation (Line 385)

**Should Fix (High Priority):**
- [ ] Remove unnecessary preference re-fetch, or cache it longer
- [ ] Add AbortController for preference fetch
- [ ] Add runtime type validation for EventSource data

**Nice to Have:**
- [ ] Normalize error messages for end users
- [ ] Use URLSearchParams for query parameter safety
- [ ] Add timeout handling for EventSource

The overall code quality is solid with good React patterns and thoughtful error handling. With the above fixes, this would be production-ready.

```typescript
  const prefRes = await fetch('/api/user/preferences')
  const prefJson = await prefRes.json()
  if (prefJson.success) {
    currentLevel = prefJson.data.readingLevel
    setReadingLevel(currentLevel)
  }
} catch (err) {
  console.error('Failed to fetch reading level:', err)
}
```
- **Problem**: Makes unnecessary API call to /api/user/preferences every time simplified view is clicked
- **Context**: There's already a separate useEffect loading preferences on mount (Lines 296-309)
- **Impact**: Network overhead, slight UX delay, inconsistent with "preference already loaded" pattern
- **Suggestion**: Only re-fetch if explicitly changed in settings, or use cached value. If re-fetching is intentional for freshness, consider debouncing

**2. No Validation of Server Response Data Types (Multiple locations)**
```typescript
if (data.total !== undefined) setTotalParagraphs(data.total)  // Line 438
if (data.paragraph !== undefined && data.text) {...}         // Line 441
if (data.done) setSimplifyStatus('ready')                     // Line 449
```
- **Problem**: No validation that `data.total` is a number, `data.paragraph` is a valid integer, or `data.text` is a string
- **Impact**: Type mismatches could silently produce unexpected UI (e.g., `totalParagraphs` could be string "100")
- **Fix**: Add runtime validation: `typeof data.total === 'number' && data.total > 0`

**3. Stale Content Display on Toggle Back (Lines 384-386)**
```typescript
setReadView('simplified')
setSimplifyError(null)
setSimplifiedContent('') // Clear stale content
```
- **Problem**: `simplifiedContent` is cleared but `simplifiedParagraphs` array isn't reset if switching from cached to new generation
- **Scenario**: User toggles to simplified (cached), then toggles to original, then toggles back to simplified (requires new generation). The old cached paragraphs might still be in array
- **Impact**: Could briefly show old paragraphs mixed with new ones during streaming
- **Fix**: Also reset: `setSimplifiedParagraphs([])` at line 385

**4. Missing Abort Signal for Preference Fetch (Lines 391-396)**
```typescript
const prefRes = await fetch('/api/user/preferences')
const prefJson = await prefRes.json()
if (prefJson.success) {
  currentLevel = prefJson.data.readingLevel
}
```
- **Problem**: If component unmounts or user clicks button again before this completes, no way to cancel the request
- **Impact**: Memory leak potential (state update on unmounted component), network request waste
- **Mitigation Exists?** Partial - unmount cleanup exists for EventSource, not for this fetch
- **Fix**: Use AbortController and pass signal to fetch

---

#### **MINOR**

**1. Loose Error Suppression (Lines 304-305, 398)**
```typescript
} catch (err) {
  console.error('Failed to load reading level:', err)
}
```
- **Pattern**: Silently continues with stale `readingLevel` if preference fetch fails
- **UX Impact**: User may not know their preference wasn't applied; simplification happens with outdated level
- **Severity**: Low - has sensible fallback (use state value), but silent failures can be confusing
- **Improvement**: Consider warning toast or UI feedback

**2. Magic String in URL Construction (Lines 403, 422)**
```typescript
`/api/section/${sectionId}/simplified?level=${currentLevel}`
`/api/section/${sectionId}/simplified/stream?level=${currentLevel}`
```
- **Issue**: Query parameter encoding not verified; if `currentLevel` has special characters, could break URL
- **Likelihood**: Very low (only enum-like values: 'elementary', 'high_school', 'undergraduate', 'graduate')
- **Best Practice**: Use `URLSearchParams` for robustness

**3. Inconsistent Success Flag Checking (Line 404, 301)**
```typescript
// Line 301 checks: if (json.success)
// Line 404 checks: if (cacheJson.success && cacheJson.data.cached)
// Both missing null/undefined checks on json.data before accessing
```
- **Risk**: If API returns `{success: true, data: null}`, accessing `json.data.cached` throws
- **Mitigation**: Unlikely in controlled API, but defensive programming missing
- **Fix**: Add `cacheJson.data?.cached`

**4. No Connection Timeout Handling (Line 421-423)**
```typescript
const eventSource = new EventSource(
  `/api/section/${sectionId}/simplified/stream?level=${currentLevel}`
)
```
- **Issue**: EventSource has default timeout, but no explicit timeout/reconnection strategy
- **Scenario**: If server responds slowly or has network latency, user sees loading indefinitely
- **Standard Practice**: Set timeout or implement manual heartbeat

**5. Inconsistent Error Messages (Lines 457, 463)**
```typescript
setSimplifyError('Connection lost. Please try again.')     // onerror handler
setSimplifyError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to generate')  // catch block
```
- **Issue**: Different error message styles; first is user-friendly, second is developer-friendly
- **UX Impact**: Confusing to user if they see technical error message
- **Fix**: Normalize error messages for user consumption

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

Guide completion of development work by presenting clear options and handling chosen workflow.

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## The Process

### Step 1: Verify Tests

**Before presenting options, verify tests pass:**

```bash
# Run project's test suite
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:**
```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]

Cannot proceed with merge/PR until tests pass.
```

Stop. Don't proceed to Step 2.

**If tests pass:** Continue to Step 2.

### Step 2: Determine Base Branch

```bash
# Try common base branches
git merge-base HEAD main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD master 2>/dev/null
```

Or ask: "This branch split from main - is that correct?"

### Step 3: Present Options

Present exactly these 4 options:

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
4. Discard this work

Which option?
```

**Don't add explanation** - keep options concise.

### Step 4: Execute Choice

#### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Switch to base branch
git checkout <base-branch>

# Pull latest
git pull

# Merge feature branch
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>

# If tests pass
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
# Push branch
git push -u origin <feature-branch>

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "<title>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<2-3 bullets of what changed>

## Test Plan
- [ ] <verification steps>
EOF
)"
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

#### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

**Don't cleanup worktree.**

#### Option 4: Discard

**Confirm first:**
```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for exact confirmation.

If confirmed:
```bash
git checkout <base-branch>
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

Then: Cleanup worktree (Step 5)

### Step 5: Cleanup Worktree

**For Options 1, 2, 4:**

Check if in worktree:
```bash
git worktree list | grep $(git branch --show-current)
```

If yes:
```bash
git worktree remove <worktree-path>
```

**For Option 3:** Keep worktree.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | ✓ | - | - | ✓ |
| 2. Create PR | - | ✓ | ✓ | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | ✓ | - |
| 4. Discard | - | - | - | ✓ (force) |

## Common Mistakes

**Skipping test verification**
- **Problem:** Merge broken code, create failing PR
- **Fix:** Always verify tests before offering options

**Open-ended questions**
- **Problem:** "What should I do next?" → ambiguous
- **Fix:** Present exactly 4 structured options

**Automatic worktree cleanup**
- **Problem:** Remove worktree when might need it (Option 2, 3)
- **Fix:** Only cleanup for Options 1 and 4

**No confirmation for discard**
- **Problem:** Accidentally delete work
- **Fix:** Require typed "discard" confirmation

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Proceed with failing tests
- Merge without verifying tests on result
- Delete work without confirmation
- Force-push without explicit request

**Always:**
- Verify tests before offering options
- Present exactly 4 options
- Get typed confirmation for Option 4
- Clean up worktree for Options 1 & 4 only

## Integration

**Called by:**
- **subagent-driven-development** (Step 7) - After all tasks complete
- **executing-plans** (Step 5) - After all batches complete

**Pairs with:**
- **using-git-worktrees** - Cleans up worktree created by that skill

message.content: This is working quite well, but I'm noticing that if I navigate away from the simplified page while it's converting, I lose all progress that was made.

content.thinking:
The user is reporting that if they navigate away while simplification is streaming, the progress is lost. This makes sense because:

1. The streaming happens client-side via EventSource
2. The cache only saves after ALL paragraphs complete successfully (by design - "only cache on full success")
3. If the user navigates away mid-stream, the EventSource closes, the stream is abandoned, and nothing is cached

This is actually working as designed in the spec - the spec says "only cache on full success" to prevent partial/corrupted content from being cached. However, it creates a poor UX when users navigate away.

Possible solutions:

1. **Save partial progress to cache** - But this contradicts the spec's "only cache on full success" rule, which was intentional to prevent incomplete content

2. **Save progress to localStorage** - Could store the partial paragraphs client-side so they can be resumed

3. **Background generation** - Start the generation server-side and let it complete even if user navigates away, then check for it when they return

4. **Warning before navigation** - Use beforeunload to warn users that generation is in progress

Let me think about the best approach:

Option 3 (background generation) is probably the best UX - the server already runs the generation in a background async task. The issue is that the EventSource connection is closed when the user navigates away, but the server-side generation continues and caches the result. 

Wait, actually looking at the streaming API code:
```typescript
;(async () => {
  // ... generation happens here
  // saves to cache after completion
})()
```

The generation DOES continue on the server even if the client disconnects! The issue is just that the client loses the streaming display. When the user returns, if they click "Simplified" again, it should find the content in cache (if the server finished generating).

But there's a timing issue - if the user navigates away mid-stream, comes back before the server finishes, and clicks Simplified again, they'll start a new generation (which wastes resources).
 
I'm considering potential user-friendly solutions that balance technical constraints with a smooth experience. The goal is to provide instant feedback and prevent unnecessary regeneration. A hybrid approach might involve storing partial progress locally while maintaining the server's full generation process. This would give users immediate visibility into ongoing work without compromising the integrity of the final cached content.

The key is creating a mechanism that allows users to see progress, resume interrupted generations, and avoid redundant processing. Exploring localStorage and connection recovery strategies could offer a seamless solution that respects both user experience and system design principles.

content.text:
Good catch. The current design only caches on full completion (to prevent storing incomplete content). When you navigate away:

1. The **server continues generating** in the background and will cache when done
2. But the **client loses the streaming progress** display

**Options to fix this:**

1. **Quick fix: Warn before navigation** - Add a `beforeunload` warning when generation is in progress

2. **Better UX: Persist partial progress** - Save streamed paragraphs to localStorage so they display instantly when you return (while still waiting for full cache)

3. **Best UX: Resume detection** - When returning to a section, detect if generation completed while away (cache hit) or show partial progress from localStorage

Which approach would you prefer? I'd recommend option 2 or 3 - they provide the smoothest experience.

1→export type ParsedQuestion = {
     2→  questionType: 'mcq' | 'prose'
     3→  questionSubtype: string
     4→  questionText: string
     5→  options?: string[]
     6→  correctAnswer?: string
     7→}
     8→
     9→export function parseQuizMarkdown(markdown: string): ParsedQuestion[] {
    10→  const blocks = markdown.split(/\n---\n/g)
    11→  const questions: ParsedQuestion[] = []
    12→
    13→  for (const block of blocks) {
    14→    const mcqMatch = block.match(/\*\*Type:\*\*\s*(one|multiple|none)/i)
    15→    if (mcqMatch) {
    16→      const options = Array.from(block.matchAll(/-\s+[A-D]\)\s+(.+)/g)).map(m => m[1].trim())
    17→      const correct = block.match(/\*\*Correct:\*\*\s*([^\n]+)/i)?.[1]?.trim()
    18→      const lines = block.split('\n')
    19→      const qLine = lines.find(line => line.trim() && !line.startsWith('###') && !line.startsWith('-') && !line.startsWith('**') && !line.startsWith('<'))
    20→      questions.push({
    21→        questionType: 'mcq',
    22→        questionSubtype: mcqMatch[1].toLowerCase(),
    23→        questionText: qLine?.trim() ?? '',
    24→        options,
    25→        correctAnswer: correct,
    26→      })
    27→      continue
    28→    }
    29→
    30→    const proseMatch = block.match(/\[Type:\s*(Adversarial|Comparative|Socratic|Synthesis)\]/i)
    31→    if (proseMatch) {
    32→      const lines = block.split('\n')
    33→      const qLine = lines.find(line => line.trim() && !line.startsWith('###') && !line.startsWith('**'))
    34→      questions.push({
    35→        questionType: 'prose',
    36→        questionSubtype: proseMatch[1].toLowerCase(),
    37→        questionText: qLine?.trim() ?? '',
    38→      })
    39→    }
    40→  }
    41→
    42→  return questions
    43→}

    21→        questionType: 'mcq',

    23→        questionText: qLine?.trim() ?? '',
    24→        options,

    42→  }
    43→

Now I understand the structure. Looking at the prompt format:

```
## Part B: Depth Questions (Prose)

Create 2-3 prose questions...

### [number]. [Type: Adversarial/Comparative/Socratic/Synthesis]

[Question text]
```

The issue is:
1. "Part B: Depth Questions (Prose)" is a header that could be getting parsed as something
2. The parser splits by `---` separators

Let me trace through the logic:
- The quiz markdown is split by `\n---\n`
- Each block is checked for MCQ or prose patterns

The problem might be:
1. "## Part B: Depth Questions (Prose)" is in a block that doesn't have `---` after it immediately
2. Or the block includes "Part B" header text which doesn't match MCQ but might partially match prose

Looking at the prose regex:
```javascript
const proseMatch = block.match(/\[Type:\s*(Adversarial|Comparative|Socratic|Synthesis)\]/i)
  || block.match(/###\s*\d+\.\s*(Adversarial|Comparative|Socratic|Synthesis)\b/i)
```

This doesn't match "Part B" but the question text extraction might be picking up the "Part B" text. Let me look at the qLine extraction:

```javascript
const qLine = lines.find(line => line.trim() && !line.startsWith('###') && !line.startsWith('**') && !line.startsWith('[Type'))
```

The issue could be that if the AI generates:
```
---

## Part B: Depth Questions (Prose)

### 5. Adversarial

Question text here...
```

Then when split by `---`, we get a block that contains both "## Part B" and "### 5. Adversarial". The prose regex matches on "### 5. 

I see the subtle parsing problem. The line filter allows headers starting with `##`, which means the section header could be mistakenly interpreted as a question line. The specific check `!line.startsWith('###')` means any two-hash header would slip through the filter, potentially causing misidentification of question lines.

The proposed solution is comprehensive: modify the filter to exclude all header lines by checking against any header prefix starting with `#`. This ensures no markdown headers interfere with question line detection.

Regarding storing raw AI output, it's strategically valuable. Preserving original responses enables future parsing improvements, simplifies debugging, and provides flexibility for expanding question types without regenerating content.

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlserver"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============ SHARED CONTENT (Library-ingested) ============

model Book {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  slug       String    @unique
  title      String
  author     String
  category   String    @default("")
  rawContent String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  ingestedAt DateTime?
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime  @updatedAt

  sections     Section[]
  userProgress UserBookProgress[]
}

model Section {
  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  bookId            String
  sectionNumber     Int
  title             String
  priority          String   @default("must")
  location          String
  startByte         Int
  endByte           Int
  wordCount         Int
  sectionContent    String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  audioUrl          String?
  podcastTranscript String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  summaryContent    String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  contentVersion    Int      @default(1)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  book              Book                @relation(fields: [bookId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  questions         Question[]
  sectionAttempts   SectionAttempt[]
  simplifiedContent SimplifiedContent[]

  @@unique([bookId, sectionNumber])
}

model Question {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  sectionId       String
  questionType    String
  questionSubtype String
  questionText    String   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  options         String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  correctAnswer   String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  explanation     String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  orderIndex      Int
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  section     Section      @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  quizAnswers QuizAnswer[]

  @@unique([sectionId, orderIndex])
}

// ============ USERS ============

model User {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  email     String?  @unique
  name      String?
  isAdmin      Boolean @default(false)
  readingLevel String  @default("undergraduate") // "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  sectionAttempts SectionAttempt[]
  bookProgress    UserBookProgress[]
}

// ============ LEARNING JOURNEY ============

model SectionAttempt {
  id                  String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId              String
  sectionId           String
  currentPhase        String    @default("read")
  blindRecall         String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  blindSubmittedAt    DateTime?
  summaryViewedAt     DateTime?
  missedPoints        String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  missedSubmittedAt   DateTime?
  recallFeedbackJson  String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  recallScore         Float?
  recallModelId       String?
  recallPromptVersion String?
  recallEvaluatedAt   DateTime?
  startedAt           DateTime  @default(now())
  completedAt         DateTime?

  user        User         @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  section     Section      @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  quizAttempt QuizAttempt?

  @@unique([userId, sectionId])
  @@index([userId])
  @@index([sectionId])
}

model QuizAttempt {
  id                   String    @id @default(cuid())
  sectionAttemptId     String    @unique
  status               String    @default("in_progress")
  totalScore           Float?
  modelId              String?
  promptVersion        String?
  thematicFeedbackJson String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  tutorNote            String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  submittedAt          DateTime?
  evaluatedAt          DateTime?
  createdAt            DateTime  @default(now())

  sectionAttempt SectionAttempt @relation(fields: [sectionAttemptId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  answers        QuizAnswer[]
}

model QuizAnswer {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  quizAttemptId String
  questionId    String
  userAnswer    String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  isCorrect     Boolean?
  score         Float?
  feedbackJson  String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  quizAttempt QuizAttempt @relation(fields: [quizAttemptId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  question    Question    @relation(fields: [questionId], references: [id], onDelete: NoAction, onUpdate: NoAction)

  @@unique([quizAttemptId, questionId])
}

// ============ PROGRESS TRACKING ============

model UserBookProgress {
  id          String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId      String
  bookId      String
  status      String    @default("not_started")
  startedAt   DateTime?
  completedAt DateTime?

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  book Book @relation(fields: [bookId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, bookId])
}

// ============ SIMPLIFIED CONTENT CACHE ============

model SimplifiedContent {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  sectionId    String
  readingLevel String   // "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
  content      String   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  section Section @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([sectionId])
  @@index([readingLevel])
  @@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlserver"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ============ SHARED CONTENT (Library-ingested) ============

model Book {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  slug       String    @unique
  title      String
  author     String
  category   String    @default("")
  rawContent String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  ingestedAt DateTime?
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime  @updatedAt

  sections     Section[]
  userProgress UserBookProgress[]
}

model Section {
  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  bookId            String
  sectionNumber     Int
  title             String
  priority          String   @default("must")
  location          String
  startByte         Int
  endByte           Int
  wordCount         Int
  sectionContent    String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  audioUrl          String?
  podcastTranscript String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  summaryContent    String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  contentVersion    Int      @default(1)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  book              Book                @relation(fields: [bookId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  questions         Question[]
  sectionAttempts   SectionAttempt[]
  simplifiedContent SimplifiedContent[]

  @@unique([bookId, sectionNumber])
}

model Question {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  sectionId       String
  questionType    String
  questionSubtype String
  questionText    String   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  options         String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  correctAnswer   String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  explanation     String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  orderIndex      Int
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt

  section     Section      @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  quizAnswers QuizAnswer[]

  @@unique([sectionId, orderIndex])
}

// ============ USERS ============

model User {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  email     String?  @unique
  name      String?
  isAdmin      Boolean @default(false)
  readingLevel String  @default("undergraduate") // "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  sectionAttempts SectionAttempt[]
  bookProgress    UserBookProgress[]
}

// ============ LEARNING JOURNEY ============

model SectionAttempt {
  id                  String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId              String
  sectionId           String
  currentPhase        String    @default("read")
  blindRecall         String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  blindSubmittedAt    DateTime?
  summaryViewedAt     DateTime?
  missedPoints        String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  missedSubmittedAt   DateTime?
  recallFeedbackJson  String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  recallScore         Float?
  recallModelId       String?
  recallPromptVersion String?
  recallEvaluatedAt   DateTime?
  startedAt           DateTime  @default(now())
  completedAt         DateTime?

  user        User         @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  section     Section      @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  quizAttempt QuizAttempt?

  @@unique([userId, sectionId])
  @@index([userId])
  @@index([sectionId])
}

model QuizAttempt {
  id                   String    @id @default(cuid())
  sectionAttemptId     String    @unique
  status               String    @default("in_progress")
  totalScore           Float?
  modelId              String?
  promptVersion        String?
  thematicFeedbackJson String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  tutorNote            String?   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  submittedAt          DateTime?
  evaluatedAt          DateTime?
  createdAt            DateTime  @default(now())

  sectionAttempt SectionAttempt @relation(fields: [sectionAttemptId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  answers        QuizAnswer[]
}

model QuizAnswer {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  quizAttemptId String
  questionId    String
  userAnswer    String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  isCorrect     Boolean?
  score         Float?
  feedbackJson  String?  @db.NVarChar(Max)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  quizAttempt QuizAttempt @relation(fields: [quizAttemptId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  question    Question    @relation(fields: [questionId], references: [id], onDelete: NoAction, onUpdate: NoAction)

  @@unique([quizAttemptId, questionId])
}

// ============ PROGRESS TRACKING ============

model UserBookProgress {
  id          String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId      String
  bookId      String
  status      String    @default("not_started")
  startedAt   DateTime?
  completedAt DateTime?

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  book Book @relation(fields: [bookId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, bookId])
}

// ============ SIMPLIFIED CONTENT CACHE ============

model SimplifiedContent {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  sectionId    String
  readingLevel String   // "undergraduate" | "masters" | "phd"
  content      String   @db.NVarChar(Max)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt

  section Section @relation(fields: [sectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([sectionId])
  @@index([readingLevel])
  @@unique([sectionId, readingLevel])
}
